question.text: The volcanoes Mount Pinatubo (pin-uh-TOO-boh) and Mount Mayon (mah-YAWN) are located on this island, the largest in the Philippines.
question.clue: This island, which sits to the south of the Babuyan Islands, is also home to the basin of the Cagayan River and Clark Air Base, which was heavily damaged by another of its volcanoes.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
swap.text: Ho Chi Minh led this nation's independence movement from France, which culminated in its victory at the Battle of Dien Bien Phu. The 1975 Fall of Saigon ended an American war in this country.
swap.answerHtml: Vietnam [or Socialist Republic of Vietnam or Cong Hoa Xa Hoi Chu Nghia Viet Nam; prompt on SRV]
swap.clue: The Le Dynasty was nominally in control of this country for over 300 years.

question.text: The later Supreme Court case New York Times Co. v. United States concerned the publication of the Pentagon Papers, which detailed U.S. involvement in this conflict. This war ended with the fall of Saigon.
question.answerHtml: Vietnam War [or Second Indochina War or Chiến tranh Việt Nam or Kháng Chiến Chống Mỹ]
question.clue: One side of this war ran a huge branching supply trail named for one side's leader that ended near Dalat, and turned the tide by breaking a traditional truce on a lunar new year holiday.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Marshal Phibun.
swap.text: After a 1932 coup in which Phibun came to power in this country governed from Bangkok, he changed its official name from Siam to a name meaning "land of the free."
swap.clue: This country was unified under the Thonburi Kingdom after the fall of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

question.leadin: This man attended the Versailles ["vair-SIGH"] Conference to advocate for equal rights for his countrymen, but was ignored.
question.text: Name this leader who led the August Revolution. This leader's namesake trail was used to supply the Tet Offensive.
question.answerHtml: Hồ Chí Minh [or Nguyễn Sinh Cung or Nguyễn Ái Quốc or Nguyễn Tất Thành or Bác Hồ; accept Ho Chi Minh Trail]
question.clue: His country's bloody 5-phase campaign for land reform began in 1954, and he was often called "Uncle" by his country's people.

swap.leadin: After coming to power, this regime announced that the start of their rule would become "Year Zero" and called for the execution of "New People" in Killing Fields.
swap.text: Name this regime led by Pol Pot during the 1970s.
swap.clue: With the help of the FUNK resistance movement under Prince Sihanouk, this government overthrew Prime Minister Lon Nol.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about 20th century Asian dictators.
question.text: This leader of the Khmer Rouge ruled as dictator of Cambodia between 1976 and 1979. His agrarian socialist policies and political purges killed over a million of his own people.
question.clue: This leader, who was referred to as "Brother Number One", helped Prince Sihanouk's ("SEE-uh-nook") attempt to return to power after he was deposed in a coup by Lon Nol.

swap.leadin: Along with future vice president Mohamad Hatta, this leader declared his country's independence following the Japanese surrender in 1945 and he resisted Dutch re-colonization efforts.
swap.text: Name this leader who aided in organizing the Bandung Conference, a precursor to the Non-Aligned Movement. This leader was a proponent of "Guided Democracy."
swap.clue: This leader hosted the meeting which led to the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement in his country's city of Bandung.

question.text: The Jementah Civil War occurred in this country, whose Islamic period began with the Kedah Sultanate. The Larut and Klang Wars led Britain to sign the Pangkor Treaty with this country,which experience unrest in the Bukit Kepong incident and May 13 race riots. For 15 points, identify this country which formed in 1963 from a union of states including Sabah and Sarawak.
question.clue: The location of the Langkasuka kingdom, its eponymous language is first attested on the Kedukan Bukit inscription.

swap.text: This figure in the coup emerged as the new ruler of Indonesia, holding office until 1998.
swap.clue: He was propelled to power by the 30 September Movement, marking the end of "Guided Democracy" and the beginning of the "New Order" period.

question.text: An earlier Ming expedition defeated pirate Chen Zuyi, who operated on this body of water. This body of water shares its name with a sultanate that fell to the Portuguese and a city overtaken in importance by Singapore.
question.clue: In 1824, the Dutch were given control over the Riau Islands in this body of water by a treaty that also broke up the Sultanate of Johor.

swap.leadin: This empire grew out of the kingdom of Chenla, and one ruler of this empire died while chasing a wild elephant.
swap.text: Name this Southeast Asian Empire founded by Jayavarman II, which also lent its name to a brutal communist government led by Pol Pot.
swap.clue: Among the landmarks in its main capital were the temples Ta Prohm, the Baphuon, and Ta Keo, the first of which was made entirely from sandstone.

question.leadin: Answer the following about archaeological museums in Indonesia.
question.text: The Balaputradeva ("bah-lah-POO-truh-DEV-uh") Museum in Palembang ("PAH-lem-bong") has many artifacts from this Sumatra-based empire, which ruled a Buddhist thalassocracy from the 8th to 12th centuries.
question.clue: The Buddhist Sailendra family ruled over both this empire and the neighboring Medang Empire for a brief period of time.

swap.leadin: Pollen analysis at this site has discredited the theory it was built to resemble a lotus flower on a lake.
swap.text: Name this site on Java's Kedu Plain where pilgrims would pass by 72 statues of the Buddha while making their way clockwise up to a stupa.

question.leadin: Some of the most vicious combat in this campaign was seen during the engagement known as the Battle of the Tennis Court.
question.text: Name this theatre of the Second World War where Operation U-Go was halted in two fierce battles in 1944 when infiltration tactics and encirclement were rendered ineffective by air supply to the defenders, while many of the attacking force's 50,000-plus casualties were caused by malnutrition and malaria.

swap.text: This kingdom was founded by U Thong, and came to dominate much of Southeast Asia from the fourteenth to eighteenth centuries. Its last king, Ekathat, was defeated by the Burmese in the 1760s.
swap.clue: Under its King Naresuan, this dynasty defeated an Eastern invader at the Battle of Nong Sarai.

question.text: This ruler's all-female police force, the Krom Klone, was described in the unreliable memoir The Romance of the Harem by Anna Leonowens, whom this ruler employed as a governess for his children.
question.answerHtml: Mongkut [or Rama IV; prompt on Rama] (The Krom Klone was generally employed by the kings of Ayutthaya and most Chakri dynasty rulers until the 1900s.)
question.clue: This ruler was forced to grant extraterritoriality and trading privileges to British subjects under the terms of the humiliating Bowring Treaty.

swap.leadin: Along with purchasing the superyacht Equanimity, funds embezzled in this scandal were ironically used to finance Red Granite Pictures's production of The Wolf of Wall Street.
swap.text: Name this scandal in which president Najib Razak and his conspirators siphoned billions from Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund.

question.leadin: The Rukunegara was instituted in part as a response to this event, which began as a reaction to the gains of the Gerakan and the Democratic Action Party, though ultimately the Alliance led by the UMNO was still in power.
question.text: Name these 1969 race riots, which forced the government to respond with the New Economic Policy under its second national plan.

swap.leadin: In 1857 Chinese laborers revolted against one of these rulers after he instituted a high opium tax, and this dynasty had its capital at Kuching.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that controlled the Miri oilfields and ruled Serawak from the mid-1800s to the mid-1900s.
swap.clue: The Japanese invasion of Borneo ended the rule of this dynasty, which began when the Sultan of Brunei rewarded the patriarch of this family with the Raj of Sarawak after crushing a tribal rebellion.
